verdict.rationale: Google Cloud's own IAM docs describe Workload Identity Federation, which gives on-premises or multicloud workloads access to Google Cloud resources through federated identities instead of service account keys. That addresses the core no-long-lived-key goal, but the pack is a single overview sentence, so the rest of the story is unproven. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of OIDC token exchange, short-lived credential issuance and lifetime, CI-specific setup (e.g. GitHub Actions or GitLab), end-to-end walkthrough documentation, any way to block or ban service account keys, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, nothing ships a long-lived key — OIDC/workload identity federation issues short-lived credentials to CI and services, documented end to end

citations.quote: Using Workload Identity Federation, you can provide on-premises or multicloud workloads with access to Google Cloud resources by using federated identities instead of a service account key.
